title: PlayStation's Founder Gets Why Fans Want Discs. He Would End Them Anyway.
excerpt: Ken Kutaragi calls discs a metaphor for owning games and the backlash a mentality issue, as Sony sets January 2028 to end PlayStation disc production.
body:
• Ken Kutaragi, the founder of PlayStation, says he understands why players are upset that Sony is ending game discs, but keeping physical media is not economically reasonable.
  • Sony plans to end physical disc production for PlayStation titles by January 2028, a shift Kutaragi called a mentality issue rather than a technical one.
  • His core argument: nobody demands physical media for a smartphone, because people trust they will keep their content. He thinks games will reach the same point.
  • The counter-argument he acknowledged: a digital purchase is a licence that can be revoked, while a disc is a copy that cannot easily be taken away.

The man who put a CD drive in the first PlayStation has weighed in on the death of the game disc, and sided, gently, with the company ending it. Ken Kutaragi, who led the creation of the first three PlayStation consoles before leaving Sony in 2007, told Video Games Chronicle that he understands the backlash to Sony's disc phaseout, but does not believe keeping discs alive makes economic sense.

"I understand that physical discs have become a metaphor for 'owning' games. I really understand that mentality," Kutaragi said, in an interview reported by Polygon.

A Mentality Issue, He Says

"I really understand [why some people are upset], but I don't think it's economically reasonable. Maybe it's a mentality issue."

https://x.com/NOTICIASENX/status/2112563530893259022 — Ken Kutaragi, founder of PlayStation

"But nobody thinks [physical media] is necessary for a networked device like a smartphone, for example, because people feel that they will keep their content. So it's a mentality," he added, speaking at the Game Republic New Horizons event in Middlesbrough, UK, according to Radio Times.

The backdrop is a hard date. Sony has said it will end physical disc production for all PlayStation titles by January 2028. Kutaragi, now 76 and chief executive of Ascent Robotics, said he had anticipated the decline of physical distribution as far back as 2006, and suggested part of the friction comes from Sony Interactive Entertainment now being staffed by people from streaming and cloud backgrounds who see PlayStation as a content terminal, not only a console.

The Ownership Problem He Did Not Dismiss

Kutaragi's sympathy is not empty, because the players' objection has a legal edge he recognised. A digital purchase is a licence, and licences can be revoked. A disc is a physical copy that cannot be taken away as easily. That asymmetry is exactly why, in his own words, discs became a metaphor for ownership in the first place.

Sony's finance leadership has argued the business will not be hurt, pointing out that most game sales are already digital. Former PlayStation executive Shuhei Yoshida has separately said he does not understand why the disc decision has become such an issue, a blunter version of the position Kutaragi expressed with more care.

What It Means for Players

For collectors in the diaspora and everywhere else, the practical window is now visible: physical releases have a production end date of January 2028. Games bought on disc before then keep working as discs do. Games bought digitally after the shift will exist entirely at the pleasure of a licence, a storefront and a server, which is precisely the trade Kutaragi says players will learn to accept, the way they did on phones.

What's Next

Kutaragi also warned that hardware itself has become, in his view, too expensive to be healthy, and mused that AI and cloud computing could one day remove the need for a console at all. Coming from the founder of the console business, that is either a prediction or a provocation. The disc decision, at least, is no longer either. It is a date.
